text:
incident-bot: ALERT detected — realtime p95/p99 regression on /v1/stream endpoint (region: us-west-2). p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~700ms in last 3m, p99 ~920ms. paging liam_oncall :rotating_light:
liam_oncall: on it. getting dashboards up now. any customer-facing hits? @anicole_cs
anicole_cs: CS reported 3 customers with increased latencies and a single revenue-impacting call for AcmeApps. Will notify account and ask for logs.
maya_sre: quick checks: tail latency spike coincides with spike in small short requests (len < 16 tokens). suspect cache churn. pulling kvcache metrics now.
jordan_eng: if kv cache is thrashing we might see cold-KV hits per request increase. pulling kvcache hit-rate and miss-rate queries.
priya_platform: I see a rolling config push to kvcache eviction policy 12:05 UTC on canary pool (recent rollout). Could that align?
incident-bot: recorded rollout: config:update:kvcache-evict@12:05:04 UTC (canary pool).
liam_oncall: timeline matches. rollback canary? we should isolate before org-wide. jordan, maya — can you reproduce locally with replay?
jordan_eng: running a small replay against canary now. code to run: ```bash
# replay small-short-requests
python tools/replay.py --trace traces/short-traffic-2026-03-15.json --target canary
```
maya_sre: dashboards: ```promql
p95_latency{endpoint="/v1/stream",region="us-west-2"}[5m]
``` shows step at 12:06. kvcache miss_rate spike: ```promql
sum(rate(kvcache_misses_total[1m])) by (pool)
``` big bump on canary pool.
liam_oncall: mitigation options: 1) rollback kvcache eviction to previous (fast) 2) route a % of traffic off canary to stable 3) enable model-variant fallback for streaming to smaller model to reduce load. Which to prioritize?
priya_platform: rollback is quickest. I can trigger rollback for canary in ~90s.
jordan_eng: if rollback is risky, do a traffic split to stable first while we validate. but rollback is small config change so safe.
anicole_cs: notifying AcmeApps now, giving ETA ~5m.
liam_oncall: do rollback, and create a short-lived traffic split if rollback doesn't reduce p99 in 3m. priya, please run rollback and post the command.
priya_platform: running rollback: ```bash
# rollback kvcache eviction policy to v1
redwoodctl config rollback --name kvcache-evict --to-version v1 --target canary
```
deploy-bot: deploy action started by priya_platform at 12:12:45 UTC, id=deploy-8823. status: in_progress
maya_sre: adding traces: tail logs show repeated small-request cold_kv loads: ```log
[12:11:52] GET /v1/stream id=xyz cold_kv_loads=7 latency=912ms
[12:11:53] GET /v1/stream id=abc cold_kv_loads=5 latency=845ms
``` looks like prefix cache eviction causing extra KV fetches per token.
jordan_eng: replay on canary confirms: p99 drops back to baseline after we prevent eviction in local test.
deploy-bot: deploy action deploy-8823 status: success at 12:13:55 UTC
liam_oncall: check metrics post-rollback — maya?
maya_sre: post-rollback p95 back to ~140ms, p99 ~160ms in us-west-2 within 40s. kvcache miss rate normalized.
liam_oncall: nice. keep watch for 15m. create a postmortem ticket and mark incident as mitigated. assign eng-runtime and platform to investigate why eviction schedule misfired with short-request workload.
jordan_eng: logging follow-ups: 1) add canary gating for kvcache eviction intensity, 2) run a canary replay load with short-request distribution, 3) consider sticky prefix caching for small requests.
priya_platform: I opened config rollback audit id=deploy-8823 and a follow-up PR to add a canary health-check for cache churn.
anicole_cs: informed customers: AcmeApps updated, support ticket #34210 created and linked.
liam_oncall: handoff to maya_sre for monitoring until 12:28 UTC. if anything flares, page SRE rotation. Good job everyone. :thumbsup:
maya_sre: I'll watch dashboards and keep a 1:1 with jordan for root cause.
liam_oncall: closing pager. Incident severity: SEV-2 (latency SLO breach briefly, mitigated).
incident-bot: Incident record created: ir-2026-03-15-4477777777, status=mitigated, mitigation=rollback kvcache-evict canary, impacted_regions=[us-west-2], affected_customers=[AcmeApps,...].
